source_text: Ut possessione aeternitatis amissa (quam quidem numquam eam per exortum sui constat habuisse), voluntas appetendae iugiter pravitatis incumberet. Et adiungis: Voluntas quae libera est in malis, libera in bonis non est; non minore plane stultitiae professione, quam profanitatis, liberum vocas, quod dicis nisi unum velle non posse.
pass_a_gloss: so that with the possession of eternity lost (which indeed it stands never to have had it through its own coming-forth), a will of seeking crookedness continually would lie upon it. And you join: A will which is free in evils, is not free in goods; with a profession plainly of no lesser stupidity than of profanity, you call free, that which you say cannot will unless one thing.

lemmas.lexica: LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS liber=free; Blaise unde liberum est abstinere
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: so that, having lost the possession of eternity, which it plainly never possessed by its origin, the will would be bent continually upon seeking wrongdoing. And you add: “The will that is free in evil is not free in good.” With a declaration of foolishness no less than of profanity, you call something free while saying it can will only one thing.

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Freedom to abstain is required for will and sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
